Since the passage of the Congressional Budget Act of 1974, Congress has only enacted all regular appropriations bills on time in four fiscal years: FY 1977, FY 1989, FY 1995, and FY 1997

Since FY 1997, Congress has consistently relied on continuing resolutions or omnibus spending packages enacted well after the October 1 deadline, meaning a complete budget has not been passed on time since then.

claim_traces.claim_text: "Lightning never strikes the same place twice."
reasoning_steps: The claim that "lightning never strikes the same place twice" is a common myth that is factually false
Lightning can and frequently does strike the exact same location multiple times, particularly tall, isolated, or conductive structures
According to the National Weather Service, prominent structures such as the Empire State Building are struck by lightning an average of 25 times per year
Furthermore, individual lightning flashes themselves often consist of multiple strokes that follow the exact same ionized channel to the ground.

This recession is driven by tidal friction, which transfers angular momentum from Earth's rotation to the Moon's orbit.
